item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Friday, 9 October 2026
item.description:
Syp fondly remembers the cheap, floppy-sized jank of Windows 3.1 games—the kind you could multitask with and never mistake for prestige gaming.

CrazyKinux and Rixx dig into EVE Online scrams, ganking, and multiboxing’s effect on faction warfare, with no easy fix in sight.

Sey’s Triple-I showcase roundup spotlights Machinarium 2, Pony Island 2, Little Prince Tyger, and Prospice with plenty of fast, trailer-hype enthusiasm.

Azuriel finishes Valheim’s Mistlands, loves the biome’s eerie spectacle, and only really loses patience when the Queen fight turns into total bug-filled nonsense.

Joel maps out an October split between spooky games like Echoes of the Eye, Symphony of the Night, Resident Evil 3, and a few books too.

Joar’s September gaming was tiny and partially untracked, but FFXIV still edged out Guild Wars 2 and WoW as the one he’s actually excited for.

Wilhelm finally lands Stardew Valley’s pesky pufferfish, completes the Community Center, and gets that rare videogame win where the nice ending beats Joja-style capitalism.

Warner shares a quiet set of Wisconsin field photos, all golden tones now with a promise of fuller fall color still on the way.

Dave Winer ricochets from NYT subscription aggravation to Ukraine anxiety, Mets-Yankees philosophy, and a fresh Web of Markdown link.

Tofutush recaps a brutal 17-credit month while plotting Moho, Live2D, Blender, and a Goose animatic powered by Hatsune Miku’s “Secret Police.”

Kelly marks Margaret Hamilton’s death with a brief, heartfelt tribute to the Apollo pioneer who helped define software engineering.

Scopique puts Mithos through its paces by building a Secret World-flavored SWADE sheet, and the conduit UI sounds like the real headache.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Thursday, 8 October 2026
item.description:
Shintar checks SWTOR /played stats and discovers her trooper main utterly dwarfs the rest of her alt roster after years in the galaxy.

Bhagpuss tours Neverness To Everness’s newly opened Pukaland, where candy-colored amusement-park fluff lands right after much darker story beats.

Emily finds Hello Kitty Island Adventure a simpler, low-stress life sim where friendship quests, collecting, and decorating cabins beat genre burnout.

Zack says Star Wars: Zero Company makes turn-based tactics approachable, while its Clone Wars mercenary story avoids leaning too hard on cameos and nostalgia.

Sweetie finds Persona 4 Golden’s Inaba murder mystery, lovable cast, and surprisingly thoughtful takes on sexuality and gender easy to see the hype in.

Wilhelm eyes LOTRO’s Wolves of Mordor pre-order with amusement and skepticism as SSG targets October 28 while keeping the release-date asterisk firmly attached.

The Chronicler runs through a Dice Commandos mission to show how its solo tactical dice puzzling feels once the stealth plans start unraveling.

Tobold revises his take on Transport Fever 3, arguing it’s less economic sim than fiddly population-growth micromanagement with weak financial tools.

UltrViolet watches the Washington Commanders implode in London, lose another quarterback, and slide toward a season that already feels like a write-off.

Ramen Junkie digs into Miniverse’s Taco Bell diorama, a surprisingly involved mini build with thick stickers, tiny fixtures, and fully assembled tacos.

Roger recounts the annoying hunt for a midrange video editor, bouncing from Corel VideoStudio to Movavi over 1440p upscaling and HDR headaches.

Cristian tackles a familiar Linux problem head-on: the community itself can scare newcomers away.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Wednesday, 7 October 2026
item.description:
Frank’s Towers of Babble demo pitches a very clever word-game-meets-tower-defense mashup where English words become towers, modifiers, and even 121,677 community-cleared levels.

Krista finds Keep Driving an easy recommendation: a laid-back early-2000s road-trip adventure with hitchhikers, multiple endings, and a soundtrack full of local indie bands.

Luna rounds up a packed September, reflects on burnout and mood, and kicks off a Spooktober backlog with Doki Doki Literature Club and Bloomtown.

Mailvaltar says Dune: Awakening’s custom settings finally make Landsraad endgame missions fun, letting the level design shine instead of the grind.

Wilhelm runs through EVE Online’s Crimson Harvest return, with faction picks, Pochven Blood Raiders, big loot-drop bonuses, and some skepticism about how newbie-friendly it is.

Aneesh posts a quick webmention test, basically a tiny hello to blyg and a check that the plumbing works.

Brennan dives into the Tildeverse, tracing how the humble tilde came to signal personal homepages, small-web culture, and “here is a person.”

Juhis is joining the latest Djangonaut Space cohort, focusing on the Django Girls+ website and planning to blog the whole open-source mentorship journey.

Mike gets keyboard scanning working for a Forth interpreter on the Sega SG-1000, turning a long-postponed hardware chore into real RetroChallenge progress.

Bruce Schneier highlights Apple’s new Reference Image system, which verifies iPhone photos as authentic while aiming to preserve photographer anonymity and image privacy.

Dave Winer dunks on Chrome, celebrates new WebSocket support in Atlantis, and pitches a stripped-down new web built from plain Markdown and RSS.

Joar gets candid about novel-writing headaches: distinct character voices, scenes that feel good but go nowhere, and resisting every cooler plot detour.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Tuesday, 6 October 2026
item.description:
Stargrace still cleared over 2 million gold in WoW despite barely posting auctions, with pets and cheap transmog finally showing signs of life.

Syp speed-runs a LOTRO housing cleanup, dives back into the endless Barrow-downs, and eyes Wolves of Mordor’s surprisingly early October launch.

Tipa digs into Malifaux 4e’s Rasputina vs. Shenlong matchup, GG1’s Map the Area strategy, and the annoyance of the newly broken iPhone app.

CrazyKinux breaks down EVE Online’s Caldari Navy Hookbill, focusing on scram-kiting, five-mid-slot flexibility, and fitting choices that actually match your plan.

Bhagpuss is deeply impressed by Neverness to Everness’s The Witch, a Salem witch trials story channeling The Crucible with unusual weight and respect.

Scopique untangles Star Citizen’s baffling pledge lockdown, where CIG now forces backers to freeze one game-access package as unmeltable and ungiftable.

Wilhelm wraps No Man’s Sky Expedition 23, a hefty 43-milestone anniversary tour through the game’s major updates that mostly samples features without too much pain.

Tobold likes Defenders of the Realm: Definitive Edition but worries its sluggish Gamefound campaign could land in the riskiest zone: barely funded.

Kelly talks candidly about down days and the coping value of reading, learning Python, and writing when heavier feelings won’t let up.

Anarchae shares a sharp links roundup on DRM-free ebooks, Twitch transcript privacy, gambling harms, labor failures, and more, plus some good job news.

Joel’s weeknotes bounce from a Penn & Teller: Fool Us binge to UNO, seafood, Land of Eem almost happening, and an accidental rom-com outing.

Warner weighs Apple’s coming Full Disk Access restrictions against AI-agent privacy risks and the collateral damage for legitimate Mac apps.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Monday, 5 October 2026
item.description:
Roger looks at why modernizing LOTRO is so hard, from decades-old code and player attachment to the strict limits of Lua plugins.

Azuriel argues Valheim’s exploration too often means slogging through RNG-gated boss clues and recycled biomes after the initial survival-crafting thrill fades.

Kimimi makes the case that Hydlide isn’t just influential 1984 RPG history; it’s still a brisk, dangerous, genuinely fun adventure today.

Ramen Junkie bounces through Fortnite FOMO, a Little Prince detour in Infinity Nikki, and bafflement at Final Fantasy XI’s old-school setup.

Emily vents about mobile games locking saved currency behind paid piggy banks, a monetization trick she finds pushy, wasteful, and immersion-killing.

Shintar is relieved WoW Forever’s regional naming should ease name sniping, but now every character needs a last name too.

Wilhelm runs through Fantasy Critic League week 40, with Toem 2 and Nighthawks nudging scores and reshuffling the publisher leaderboard.

The Chronicler rounds up teaching, strategy, and example-play materials for Plantagenet, highlighting its Wars of the Roses spin on Levy & Campaign.

Tan checks in with a hectic life update, a haiku publication, Nier: Automata progress, and Aristotle chats that eventually drift toward AI.

Cristian shares a simple photo post: ducklings at Lacul Gheorgheni for the100pics.

Bruce Schneier points to another AI-assisted crack of a historic cipher, this one from 1809 and tied to Napoleon’s nephew.

Dave Winer praises Claude’s code-reading chops, enjoys blogging with Frontier again, and says climate change is the bigger existential threat than AI.
